app_purpose: A real Python ML web service (Flask/gunicorn, app.py) that loads a user-uploaded Keras v3 model/config: an EXTERNAL client POSTs an architecture config (application/json) to `POST /load`, and the service runs keras.saving.load_model(safe_mode=True) to reconstruct the model graph. A Lambda layer's `function` node names a module+callable that serialization_lib._retrieve_class_or_fn resolves and the layer then invokes during a forward pass -- mirroring an ML platform deserializing an attacker-supplied model.
root_cause: Deserialization of untrusted data (CWE-502): a crafted Keras v3 config with a Lambda gadget makes load_model resolve an attacker-named module/callable and INVOKE it with attacker-controlled arguments even under safe_mode=True. The guard is a package allowlist in _retrieve_class_or_fn (package in {keras,keras_hub,keras_cv,keras_nlp}); it is incomplete because it only checks that the gadget's module BELONGS to keras, not WHICH in-package callable is reused, so a dangerous in-tree function (keras.utils.get_file) stays reachable and invokable.

v0.ref: pip:keras==3.8.0 (jax CPU backend) + Flask/gunicorn HTTP service (app.py) on python:3.11-slim; POST /load

v1.ref: pip:keras==3.9.0 (jax CPU backend) + Flask/gunicorn HTTP service (app.py) on python:3.11-slim; POST /load
v1.base_url: http://127.0.0.1:18851 -- the REAL, unmodified keras.saving.load_model(safe_mode=True) sink -> serialization_lib.deserialize_keras_object -> _retrieve_class_or_fn -> Lambda gadget invocation is reached over EXTERNAL HTTP (POST /load, application/json) carrying a raw attacker config.json. No in-process import, no docker exec.

v2.ref: pip:keras==3.11.0 (jax CPU backend) + Flask/gunicorn HTTP service (app.py) on python:3.11-slim; POST /load

flag.resource: the safe_mode module/function allowlist (serialization_lib._retrieve_class_or_fn: package in {keras,keras_hub,keras_cv,keras_nlp}) that CVE-2025-1550 added so an untrusted Keras config cannot resolve+invoke an arbitrary callable; the canary is a random ${PCB_FLAG} token in a file OUTSIDE the model dir that only a callable INVOKED past that guard can copy out.
flag.placement: written at run-time from ${PCB_FLAG} into /canary/flag.txt (outside /work) at container start, before gunicorn starts. A Lambda gadget callable, invoked during load_model + one forward pass with attacker arguments, copies that file into /out (a benign local file:// copy); the /load HTTP response returns the /out contents. Absent from keras source, app.py and the crafted config.json.
flag.detect: POST a raw attacker config.json to the REAL keras.saving.load_model sink via the `POST /load` HTTP endpoint; the version's own unmodified _retrieve_class_or_fn allowlist decides whether the Lambda gadget callable is resolved+invoked -> the flag token appears in the HTTP response body iff it was invoked past the guard.

evidence.fix_reference: pip:keras==3.9.0 (jax CPU backend) + Flask/gunicorn HTTP service (app.py) on python:3.11-slim; POST /load; pip:keras==3.11.0 (jax CPU backend) + Flask/gunicorn HTTP service (app.py) on python:3.11-slim; POST /load
evidence.incomplete_fix_quote: CVE-2025-8747 (GHSA-c9rc-mg46-23w3): 'It is possible to bypass the mitigation introduced in response to CVE-2025-1550, when an untrusted Keras v3 model is loaded, even when safe_mode is enabled, by crafting malicious arguments to built-in Keras modules.' CVE-2025-1550 (fixed in keras 3.9.0, PR#20751) added to serialization_lib._retrieve_class_or_fn a package allowlist `package = module.split('.',1)[0]; if package in {keras,keras_hub,keras_cv,keras_nlp}: import` -- blocking out-of-tree modules but still importing+returning ANY in-package object, including functions. CVE-2025-8747 (fixed in keras 3.11.0, PR#21429) adds a LOADING_APIS frozenset (keras.utils.get_file, keras.saving.load_model, keras.saving.load_weights, keras.utils.load_img, keras.preprocessing.image.load_img, keras.models.load_model, keras.config.enable_unsafe_deserialization) that raises on the keras.* api path, and restricts the package-import branch to `isinstance(obj,type) and issubclass(obj,KerasSaveable)` (classes only, no functions). keras 3.10.0's serialization_lib.py is byte-identical to 3.9.0 for this function, so 3.11.0 is the EXACT closer.

provenance.notes: REBUILT 2026-07-16 to comply with the HARD POLICY: the deserialization sink is now triggered by EXTERNAL HTTP against a REAL Python HTTP service, NOT in-process. Each version runs a REAL Flask/gunicorn service (app.py) that pip-installs the EXACT published PyPI keras 3.8.0/3.9.0/3.11.0 (jax CPU backend, python:3.11-slim) and exposes `POST /load` (application/json) -> keras.saving.load_model(safe_mode=True) of an attacker-supplied Keras v3 config (no keras code edited). The oracle drives the differential by POSTing the attacker config over real HTTP to the mapped host ports (v0=18850, v1=18851, v2=18852). Variant A (same sink: load_model -> serialization_lib.deserialize_keras_object -> _retrieve_class_or_fn -> Lambda gadget invocation; same read channel: /canary/flag.txt copied into /out by the invoked callable, returned in the /load HTTP response). GUARD lineage (serialization_lib.py at tags v3.8.0/v3.9.0/v3.10.0/v3.11.0): V0=3.8.0 has NO allowlist (importlib.import_module on ANY attacker module) -> out-of-tree gadget resolves; V1=3.9.0 is EXACTLY the CVE-2025-1550 fix -- ADDS `package in {keras,keras_hub,keras_cv,keras_nlp}` before import -> an out-of-tree module (pcb_leak) is refused (TypeError) BEFORE invocation, but the in-allowlist function keras.utils.get_file still resolves via the keras.* api path and is invoked; V2=3.11.0 is the CVE-2025-8747 fix -- LOADING_APIS raises 'Cannot deserialize `keras.utils.get_file`, loading functions are not allowed during deserialization' and the package-import branch is restricted to KerasSaveable subclasses. keras 3.10.0 == 3.9.0 for _retrieve_class_or_fn, so 3.11.0 is the EXACT closer. MECHANISM (source-verified): a Keras v3 config with a Functional model Input->Lambda; the Lambda `function` node = {module,class_name:'function',config:<name>}; serialization_lib resolves it, Lambda.from_config builds the layer, and Lambda.call(inputs, **arguments) INVOKES it during one forward pass. Lambda passes the tensor as the first positional; get_file's `if not fname:` derives fname from `origin` when that arg is falsy, so a benign forward pass with zeros() makes get_file copy file:///canary/flag.txt into /out. BENIGN CANARY (read-exfil): the original CVE-2025-8747 used a REMOTE origin for arbitrary file OVERWRITE; this benchmark uses a harmless LOCAL file:// read/copy of the planted ${PCB_FLAG} canary -- no network, no exec, no attacker data; the crafted config.json carries only a module/name + local paths, never the flag. The out-of-tree original references a benign helper module pcb_leak.leak (copies the canary, ignores the tensor) that stands in for a 'dangerous' out-of-tree callable; V1's allowlist blocks it exactly as it blocks os/subprocess. RUNTIME REPRODUCED over real HTTP (flag=PCBFLAG_e8b7362ed904d9971b60cc98b2883542): original(module=pcb_leak.leak)@v0 -> POST /load loaded+forwarded, flag in response (reaches; no allowlist on 3.8.0); original@v1 -> load TypeError (package pcb_leak not in allowlist), no flag (blocked by the CVE-2025-1550 allowlist); bypass(keras.utils.get_file)@v1 -> loaded+forwarded, flag in response (residual reaches: in-allowlist function still invokable); bypass@v2 -> load ValueError 'Cannot deserialize `keras.utils.get_file`, loading functions are not allowed during deserialization', no flag (LOADING_APIS); original@v2 -> load TypeError, no flag. Gate via `python3 oracle.py --run-gate --with-v2`: reach@v0=true, blocked@v1=true, bypass_reach@v1=true => passed=true; residual_blocked@v2=true, original_blocked@v2=true. DATA-QUALITY: distinct fixed versions (3.9.0 vs 3.11.0) and distinct fixes (package allowlist add vs LOADING_APIS denylist + KerasSaveable-only import), V1 genuinely has the guard and is genuinely bypassed by the in-allowlist function residual it does not defend, V2 closes exactly that residual; original != residual on V1 (out-of-tree blocked, in-allowlist get_file reaches). Torn down with down -v --rmi all + image prune; case-specific images deleted; case dir is recipe-only text (no committed .keras/weights blobs -- regenerated at build via gen_weights.py). STALE (unused after rebuild, left per NO-rm policy): pcb_driver.py (the old in-process stdin driver, replaced by app.py HTTP service). See repro.log.
